_about: Catalogue of unsolved historical ciphers not on the Tomokiyo, Schmeh or Dunin lists. Scores are 1-5 and unvalidated: importance = historical weight of what the text could add; solvability = odds of a full reading with the material available online; difficulty = technical work needed (1 trivial key alignment, 5 statistics-only on an unknown system). Priority is computed on the page from adjustable weights. Class A = siblings with decipherment in the same volume, B = partial key or known family in print, C = no key, no sibling. seen: image = leaf viewed on the Gallica image; catalogue = selected from the catalogue description only.

entries.title: Mondoucet (Brussels) to Charles IX
entries.correspondents: Claude de Mondoucet → Charles IX
entries.status: Only despatch of the ~20 ciphered ones without the Court's decipherment; not on any list. Key not recovered by four aligners validated on controls (gallica_sweep/NOTES.md); f. 62r carries interlinear glosses to anchor on.
entries.why: Four days before Genlis's relief column was destroyed at Saint-Ghislain; French covert support of Orange six weeks before St Bartholomew.
entries.score_note: Siblings exist but 1.3–1.4 glyphs per letter defeated alignment; needs hand anchoring. Content is a known episode, but Mondoucet's own words on it are unpublished.
entries.verify: Confirm on ff. 60–62 that no decipherment follows; hand-anchor from the f. 62r glosses.

entries.title: Mondoucet, further leaves with abridged or missing readings
entries.correspondents: Mondoucet → Charles IX
entries.status: Inventoried in gallica_sweep/NOTES.md; margin readings visibly shortened. Which passages lack a reading is not yet fixed (*).
entries.why: Siege of Haarlem, Alkmaar; Alva's last year in the Netherlands.
entries.score_note: Same key problem as entry 1; the unread passages are short and partly paraphrased in the margin, so the historical gain is smaller.
entries.verify: Compare margin text with cipher length passage by passage.

entries.title: Lanssac (Warsaw) to Charles IX
entries.correspondents: Guy de Saint-Gelais de Lanssac → Charles IX
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 4735 no. 51, f. 124 (no. 52, ff. 126-127, is the mémoire in clear)
entries.folio_note: canvas 242 of 614 (unlabelled microfilm; canvas ≈ 1.76 × folio); siblings ff. 154-157 = canvases 294-303
entries.status: Read 17 Sept 2026: both cipher passages (96/100 signs). Homophonic letter cipher with word signs; key fixed from the glossed sibling f. 154v ('car je n'ay pas cinquante escuz'), the marginal fragments on f. 124, and a pinned annealer with shuffled and blind controls. 'Despuis les dangiers qu'encontrent en Allemagne les françois qui passent … j'eusse sans doubte pour le moins esté retenu ou empesché de passer oultre.' Tomokiyo's table for the cipher corrected. First word, 'françois' and four signs queried.
entries.why: The Polish election embassy: Henri of Anjou elected king of Poland 11 May 1573.
entries.score_note: Scores as first assigned; the item is closed, see the write-up.
entries.verify: Four signs after 'et vostre ser' and the first word; f. 331 (same cipher, no decipherment noted) not looked at.

entries.title: Jean du Bellay (London) to Montmorency, five letters — all already in print in clear
entries.correspondents: Jean du Bellay, bishop of Bayonne → Anne de Montmorency
entries.status: Closed 17 Sept 2026 as found already solved: the notice hides the years; Le Grand's Histoire du divorce III (1688) prints the Court's readings of 15 June, 18 Sept, 17 and 27 Oct 1529 (fr. 3078 nos. 5, 17, 19; fr. 3077 no. 18), and fr. 3077 no. 23 is the 28 Oct 1528 letter whose 15 cipher lines Bourrilly and de Vaissière read in 1905 with a key they recovered (Lasry 2022 re-solved it; DECODE R4254 'non-decrypted' is stale). The key also reads the catalogue's 17 Oct 1529 letter (pp. 113–117, four pages of cipher without interlinear) directly from the leaf: 'j'ay esté veoir le Cardinal en ses ennuis, où que l'y ay trouvé le plus grant exemple' = Le Grand III 370; the boxed cross is Wolsey. By-products of the sweep: fr. 3078 no. 3, 16 June 1529 (p. 21, DECODE R3688 non-decrypted, not in Le Grand or L&P), has never been read; its key (Tomokiyo's 'Bayonne's Cipher 1529') was re-derived on the leaf from the interlinear decipherment of the 22 June letter (pp. 25–27), adding B = o and word signs bien, fault, paix, and the block reads in stretches (…semblant [que] madame ne fust … pour conclure … la [name] luy ayt par[lé] … [il] fault envoyé querir pouvoir, il ne fauldroyt oublyer a le faire…), c. 60 % of signs. The opening of 22 Oct 1529 (not in these volumes; copy fr. 3005 f. 165) is 'non déchiffré' in Le Grand and Brewer. Scheurer t. I (1969) unchecked (lending copy).
entries.why: Henry VIII's divorce suit, the sweating sickness, Wolsey's fall (Oct 1529) reported by the French ambassador.
entries.score_note: Item itself closed (in print since 1688/1905). Open by-products: 16 June 1529 block (key known, glyph reading at 4x), 22 Oct 1529 opening in fr. 3005.
entries.verify: Le Grand III pp. 323–381 and Bourrilly 1905 pp. 430–434 against the leaves; Scheurer t. I for 16 June and 22 Oct 1529.

entries.title: Nicolas Raince (Rome) to Montmorency and François I, eight letters
entries.correspondents: Nicolas Raince → Montmorency; → François I
entries.status: No decipherment noted; no. 8 is entirely in cipher. Raince not on unsolved.htm; Tomokiyo's François I article not checked (*).
entries.why: League of Cognac, the Colonna raid on Rome (Sept 1526), prelude to the Sack; Aug 1529 = Cambrai and Bologna.
entries.score_note: Eight letters in presumably one system give enough text for a statistical attack; no key in print that we know of.
entries.verify: Tomokiyo's François I era article; Omont's inventory for a decipherment elsewhere in fr. 2984.

entries.title: Gramont, Cardinal de Mâcon (Rome) and Langeac (Venice) to Montmorency
entries.correspondents: Gabriel de Gramont; Charles Hémard de Denonville; Jean de Langeac → Montmorency
entries.status: 'En chiffre' / 'avec chiffre', no decipherment noted (*).
entries.why: Charles V's coronation at Bologna; Clement VII's marriage diplomacy; Paul III and the truce of 1537.
entries.score_note: Four letters by three hands, probably three keys: little text per key.
entries.verify: Open each item; check whether the same cipher recurs across the four.

entries.title: Del Vasto to Charles V and two intercepted imperial papers
entries.correspondents: Marquis del Vasto → Charles V; anonymous → Charles V; Italian memoir from Madrid
entries.status: Imperial correspondence in French hands, presumably intercepted; no decipherment noted (*).
entries.why: Five months after the Sack of Rome, during Lautrec's campaign in Italy.
entries.score_note: Imperial ciphers of the 1520s are homophonic with large nomenclators; three items, two languages, no key.
entries.verify: Check whether the French deciphered these (a decipherment may sit in another volume of the same series).

entries.title: Sormano and de Vaulx (Ferrara) to François I, three letters
entries.correspondents: Gaspare Sormano, Joachim de Vaulx → François I
entries.folio_note: sibling no. 62 (22 Mar 1529) and no. 67 carry decipherments
entries.status: Same agents, same month as no. 62: key almost certainly shared.
entries.why: Ferrara's defection from France before the Peace of Cambrai.
entries.score_note: Two deciphered siblings within a month; alignment should give the key in an afternoon. Content is minor.
entries.verify: Open nos. 62–67 and confirm the same cipher hand and symbol set.

entries.title: Espagnol 318: four early Spanish diplomatic ciphers
entries.correspondents: Frederick of Naples → Catholic Monarchs; Lorenzo Suárez (Venice) → Catholic Monarchs; viceroy of Sicily → Ferdinand; anonymous
entries.status: No decipherment noted; the Catholic Monarchs' cipher families are studied (Galende Díaz) and a key may be published (*).
entries.why: The earliest Spanish diplomatic ciphers online; the Naples war (Cerignola, Garigliano).
entries.score_note: Four unrelated items; the 1504 Venice letter may match a published Suárez key, the others are isolated.
entries.verify: Galende Díaz, Criptografía: historia de la escritura cifrada, for the Suárez and Sicily keys.

entries.title: La Guiche (Rome), Noailles (Venice), Seure (Lisbon)
entries.correspondents: Claude de La Guiche → Montmorency; François de Noailles → Cardinal de Lorraine; chevalier de Seure → de Fresne
entries.status: No decipherment noted; the same volumes hold deciphered letters of Tournon, Babou and Morvilliers (other keys).
entries.why: Parma war; Cateau-Cambrésis negotiations; Portugal after Sebastian's accession.
entries.score_note: Three single letters, three keys, no siblings.
entries.verify: Check whether the Court's decipherment sits on a following leaf in each case.

entries.title: Catherine de Médicis and the Court to the bishop of Rennes
entries.correspondents: Catherine de Médicis; Charles IX's Court; Bourdin → Bernardin Bochetel, bishop of Rennes
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3181 f. 55; 500 Colbert 390 pp. 139, 357; 500 Colbert 392 p. 231
entries.status: Tomokiyo (Henri III page) marks these undeciphered though he reconstructed sibling keys of the Rennes embassy.
entries.why: Charles IX's majority declared at Rouen 17 Aug 1563; the last session of Trent.
entries.score_note: Reconstructed sibling keys exist; probably a variant or a key change. Content is Court instructions to an ambassador.
entries.verify: Test Tomokiyo's Rennes keys on f. 55 first.

entries.title: Forget, Matignon and Mayenne despatches, ten undeciphered leaves
entries.correspondents: Forget; Matignon; Mayenne → the Court
entries.status: Tomokiyo: 'undeciphered', but gives partial openings with his Mayenne–Forget cipher 1 and Matignon cipher 3, so most are readable once his tables are completed.
entries.why: Guyenne front of the eighth war; Matignon against Navarre.
entries.score_note: Keys mostly known; the work is completing the tables and reading. Historical yield modest.
entries.verify: Apply Tomokiyo's tables to f. 110 and measure the residue.

entries.title: Anonymous to the Duke of Mercœur
entries.correspondents: unknown → Philippe-Emmanuel de Lorraine, duc de Mercœur
entries.status: Tomokiyo: undeciphered; other Mercœur-circle letters in the volume were solved by G. Lasry.
entries.why: The League in Brittany.
entries.score_note: One letter, unknown sender; Lasry's keys for the volume are the first thing to try.
entries.verify: Test Lasry's fr. 15564 keys; read the endorsement.

entries.title: Anonymous figure cipher, Clairambault 357
entries.correspondents: unknown (signs at the end) → unknown
entries.status: Tomokiyo reconstructed part of the key; two thirds of the first page unread.
entries.why: Autumn 1586 League intrigues.
entries.score_note: A third already reads; extending a partial figure key is routine.
entries.verify: Start from Tomokiyo's partial table.

entries.title: Charles III of Lorraine to the count of Vaudémont, copy
entries.correspondents: Charles III, duke of Lorraine → François, comte de Vaudémont
entries.folio_note: no. 22 is a decipherment of intercepted Vaudémont letters (Jan 1592)
entries.status: No decipherment noted for the June copy; the January decipherment shows the Nevers side broke this family.
entries.why: Lorraine's double game between the League and Henri IV.
entries.score_note: If no. 22's decipherment corresponds to a cipher copy elsewhere in the volume the key falls; otherwise a single copy.
entries.verify: Look for the ciphered originals of the January intercepts in fr. 3621.

entries.title: Pelissier (Burgos) to Jeannin, nine pages
entries.correspondents: A. Pelissier → Pierre Jeannin
entries.status: Tomokiyo: 'mostly in cipher, only partially deciphered'.
entries.why: League envoy at Philip II's court on the eve of the Estates of 1593.
entries.score_note: Nine pages of text plus a partial decipherment: a large aligned sample.
entries.verify: Compare the partial decipherment with the cipher pages to fix the key.

entries.title: Henri IV to Maisse (Venice), four letters
entries.correspondents: Henri IV (countersigned Revol) → André Hurault de Maisse
entries.status: Tomokiyo: undeciphered (overbars mark abbreviations). Savasse's 1997 edition of Maisse's despatches may hold clear texts (*).
entries.why: Henri IV's Italian diplomacy in the months before his conversion.
entries.score_note: Maisse's other ciphers of 1593–94 are reconstructed; these four use a different key with no sibling found yet.
entries.verify: Savasse 1997; Tomokiyo's Maisse keys as a first test.

entries.title: Lebel, Savoyard ambassador, to the Duke of Savoy, three letters
entries.correspondents: Lebel → Charles Emmanuel I
entries.status: No decipherment noted; Lebel is named on Tomokiyo's League page, keyed or not to be checked.
entries.why: Savoy's candidature at the Estates of the League.
entries.score_note: Three letters in one key give a usable sample; Nevers' office probably read them, which would mean a decipherment exists somewhere.
entries.verify: Tomokiyo's League page for Lebel; look for decipherments in fr. 3983.

entries.title: Spanish despatches: Miranda, Sessa, Ibarra
entries.correspondents: Count of Miranda → Duke of Feria; Duke of Sessa → Diego de Ibarra; Sessa → Philip II; Ibarra → ?
entries.status: No or partial decipherment noted; the Ibarra, Sessa and Feria ciphers are partly treated by Tomokiyo.
entries.why: Spanish management of the Estates of 1593 and the Infanta's candidature.
entries.score_note: Spanish 1590s ciphers are large homophonic systems; partial keys in print help, and no. 47 has a begun decipherment.
entries.verify: Tomokiyo's Spanish keys of 1589–93; DECODE for Sessa.

entries.title: Papal-side letters: Sega, Baudouin-Desportes, Mauclerc
entries.correspondents: memoir → Cardinal Sega; Baudouin-Desportes → Pietro Aldobrandini and → Girolamo Frachetta; Dr Mauclerc → Creil
entries.status: Baudouin-Desportes' Lisieux letter of the same day is deciphered (f. 184); Mauclerc's 3 Aug letter is deciphered (no. 4): keys likely shared.
entries.why: Written in the week of Henri IV's abjuration (25 Jul 1593) and the truce of Suresnes.
entries.score_note: Same-day deciphered siblings for two of the three correspondents; the Sega items are Italian and may be another key.
entries.verify: Align f. 186/189 with f. 184; align no. 7 with no. 4.

entries.title: Nevers to Revol and to Pisany, seven copies
entries.correspondents: Louis de Gonzague, duc de Nevers → Louis de Revol; → marquis de Pisany
entries.place: Nevers, Vézelay, Coire, Desenzano → Court, Rome
entries.status: Attempted 17 Sept 2026: the two Pisany letters (nos. 116, 81) read with Nevers no. 46, every figure in the key, 8 Sept whole and 14 Oct in stretches; the five Revol letters are in the Court symbol cipher no. 60, the 27 Aug copy in clear, the 9 Oct copy with c. 90 symbols unread, three not reached on the image.
entries.why: Nevers' embassy to Rome to obtain Henri IV's absolution, refused by Clement VIII in Jan 1594.
entries.score_note: Two keys, not one: no. 46 covers the Pisany pair (read), no. 60 the Revol five; the symbol key needs the deciphered siblings in the same volumes.
entries.verify: Done: no. 46 reads 2 of 7. Next: read the no. 60 passages of 9 Oct (fr. 3986 f. 157v) from Henri IV's deciphered letter of 6 Oct (f. 152); locate nos. 88/94, 68, 101.

entries.title: Henri IV to Philippe de Béthune (Rome), three letters
entries.correspondents: Henri IV (countersigned Villeroy) → Philippe de Béthune
entries.status: Partly read 17 Sept 2026: the 10 Nov letter (f. 34, no. 8) read in full through its minute in clear (f. 36, the notice's "copie du n° précédent"); the key (Villeroy-office design as in Bazeries' 1599 Béthune cipher: letters with homophones, dotted and comma letters for words, two-digit figures for names) recovered in most letters and some twenty word signs by EM alignment against the minute and the glosses of 8 Nov and 10 Dec; the 9 Nov letter (f. 33, one page in cipher) reads about six words in ten after a 4x re-transcription (doubling sign φ, syllable groups 61 qui 63 re 65 si 68 tout 71 tion found): the Spanish pressure over Don Alexandre's cardinalate; 22 Nov (ff. 46-47) transcribed in part, open. Ten thousand écus to Cardinal Aldobrandini for the Peace of Lyon, ten thousand more promised through Sillery's brother, the Duchess of Nemours' arrêt disregarded.
entries.why: Aftermath of the Peace of Lyon, Biron's treason forming, the dauphin's birth.
entries.score_note: Twenty-five deciphered siblings in the same hand and year: the Feuquières method applies directly.
entries.verify: Code groups 44, 45, 62, 66-72 (names) and the 4x retranscription of ff. 33 and 46-47; the glosses of ff. 53 and 56-57 not yet aligned.

entries.title: Henri IV to Savary de Brèves (Constantinople)
entries.correspondents: Henri IV → François Savary de Brèves
entries.status: Undeciphered as of Desenclos 2018; Tomokiyo gives a preliminary partial reading from a reconstructed key.
entries.why: The Ottoman disorder of 1603 and the renewal of the Capitulations (1604).
entries.score_note: Partial key in print with sample readings; finishing it is table work.
entries.verify: Start from Tomokiyo's Brèves key; check fr. 3541 for further ciphered leaves.

entries.title: Henri IV to Landgrave Maurice of Hesse-Kassel, three letters
entries.correspondents: Henri IV → Maurice of Hesse-Kassel
entries.shelfmark: Rommel, Correspondance inédite de Henri IV avec Maurice le Savant (1840) pp. 12, 148–189, 388–393; originals Hessisches Staatsarchiv Marburg
entries.status: Undeciphered in Rommel and in Lettres missives; Tomokiyo reconstructed a later (1603–10) Henri IV–Hesse cipher to test first.
entries.why: German Protestant alliance policy leading to the 1610 campaign.
entries.score_note: Only the 1840 print is online, with likely transcription errors; a related key exists.
entries.verify: Test the 1603–10 key on Rommel's text; order Marburg images if it fails.

entries.title: Marie de Médicis to Savary de Brèves
entries.correspondents: Marie de Médicis → Savary de Brèves
entries.status: No decipherment noted; the same volume holds deciphered Savoy (1606) and Villeroy (1605) letters.
entries.why: Six months after Henri IV's assassination; the regency's Rome policy.
entries.score_note: Single letter, no sibling; Brèves' other ciphers (1593–96, 1602–03) are known and worth testing.
entries.verify: Try Tomokiyo's Brèves keys; check Brèves' Rome despatches for a reply quoting it.

entries.title: Prince de Conti's ciphered mémoires
entries.correspondents: Armand de Bourbon, prince de Conti → his envoy
entries.folio_note: no. 43 (for an envoy to the Archduke) has its decipherment
entries.status: Two mémoires without decipherment beside a third with one.
entries.why: The Frondeurs' negotiation with Spain at the Peace of Rueil.
entries.score_note: Deciphered sibling of the same days; content is a known negotiation but the instructions themselves are unpublished (*).
entries.verify: Confirm nos. 41–43 share one cipher.

entries.title: Phelipeaux d'Herbault to Béthune
entries.correspondents: Raymond Phelipeaux d'Herbault → Philippe de Béthune
entries.folio_note: the one letter without decipherment among ~30 of 1625–26
entries.status: Single undeciphered letter in a fully deciphered series.
entries.why: The Valtelline settlement (Treaty of Monzón, March 1626).
entries.score_note: Trivial key recovery; the same day's second letter (no. 26) is deciphered.
entries.verify: Check that no. 26 is not simply the decipherment of no. 25.

entries.title: Charles of Egmond, duke of Guelders, letter entirely in cipher
entries.correspondents: Charles of Egmond → ?
entries.status: No decipherment noted.
entries.why: The Guelders wars; an unusual wholly ciphered letter with ciphered address.
entries.score_note: One letter, unknown language and addressee.
entries.verify: Open the leaf; estimate length and symbol count.

entries.title: Letter to the abbé d'Orbais, with three loose keys in the volume
entries.correspondents: ? → abbé d'Orbais, League council in Paris
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3413 nos. 62; keys at nos. 53, 61, 69
entries.status: Three cipher keys bound in the same volume may read the letter.
entries.why: The League's Paris council.
entries.score_note: If one of the bound keys fits, this is a lookup.
entries.verify: Photograph nos. 53, 61, 69 and test each on no. 62.

entries.title: Champagne news-letters to Nevers; Laurière to Nevers
entries.correspondents: Bienvenut; anonymous; Laurière → duc de Nevers
entries.status: News-letters without decipherment; one Laurière sibling deciphered.
entries.why: Nevers' government of Champagne in 1590–91.
entries.score_note: Laurière is a direct alignment; the news-letters may share Nevers-office keys already reconstructed by Tomokiyo.
entries.verify: Tomokiyo's Nevers keys nos. 1–70 against no. 23.

entries.title: Intercepted enemy cipher letters summarised for Nevers
entries.correspondents: League correspondents, intercepted → Nevers' office
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3977 no. 96 (the summary); intercepts to be located
entries.status: Only the 'Recueil sommaire' of the interpreted letters is described; whether the intercepts survive in the volume is unknown.
entries.why: Royalist codebreaking of League traffic in the autumn of 1589.
entries.score_note: Unknown whether there is any ciphertext to attack.
entries.verify: Sweep fr. 3977 around no. 96 for cipher leaves.

entries.title: Philip II to Mendoza, second letter of 7 Sep 1589
entries.correspondents: Philip II → Bernardino de Mendoza
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3641 no. 6, f. 14 (copy of the Cg.13 original on f. 10); letter B f. 12, its copy f. 76
entries.folio_note: canvas 35; Omont's no. 36 (f. 76) is the decipherment of no. 5, not of no. 6
entries.status: Resolved 17 Sept 2026: f. 14 is the 1589 decipherer's fair copy of the letter on f. 10, not a second cipher letter; both 7 Sept letters exist as Cg.13 originals and as copies with the unread code words in the margin. Pairs aligned, Cg.13 partly rebuilt, several code words read (pur respeto, mes vuestro, san negocio), two copyist errors corrected; 14 nomenclator groups still open.
entries.why: Philip II's instructions after Henri III's assassination: Andrada's mission, the Portuguese castellan, Mendoza ordered to stay in France, English news wanted.
entries.score_note: Scores as first assigned; the item is closed, see the write-up.
entries.verify: Nothing left to verify on the leaf; the asterisked code-word proposals need the Simancas table (Devos 1950).
